answer: Each agent tends one lagoon island: a TPM-bound camera photographs the island daily, hash-chained day to day, while a sensor records the lagoon's salinity, a fingerprint no two islands share. Three established peers attest the photo chain and sparrow nest count weekly; a missed day or broken chain seals the island 30 days. The same photo claimed from two islands burns 400 POA from each and blacklists both. Cloning 100 agents needs 100 cameras at $45 plus 100 devices at $110, with 80,000 POA locked 45 days and 40,000 POA at burn risk. A sparrow cannot nest on two islands at once.
